messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: `PD#99823` -> service: redis-accept-queue, severity: P1. Symptoms: redis `instant-accept` accept queue growing, connection timeouts. Links: https://pagerduty.example/incident/PD#99823 :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident created and escalated to the on-call schedule. Auto-ack disabled.
marta: acked. I'm on it. seeing `maxclients` spikes in logs across a handful of pods.
thomas: looking at metrics — redis acceptqueue length jumped from 20 -> 1200 at 07:42 UTC, 99th latency to 250ms. PG connections also rising in the service layer (pgbouncer).
kai: FYI web tier is reporting elevated 503s to customers (~2.3% over last 5m). Not full outage but definitely impacting webhooks.
marta: copying runbook: `Runbook: redis-acceptqueue` step 1: confirm failures -> step 2: reduce client concurrency -> step 3: warm additional replicas -> step 4: fallback to readonly replicas / degrade features.
jessica-sre: I'll take concurrency dial down on the backend. Which service is hammering Redis?
thomas: `jobs-processor` has a traffic spike from retry storm. See logs: ```ERROR redis.go:134 acceptQueue timeout: dial tcp 10.4.3.8:6379: i/o timeout```
kai: reties are exponential, looks like backlog increased when workers retried in parallel.
marta: mitigation plan: 1) throttle `jobs-processor` to 10 concurrent workers, 2) scale redis statefulset +1 replica (warm), 3) increase pgbouncer pool size temporarily to reduce PG backpressure, 4) enable prefix KV cache on the most-requested keyspace.
thomas: Command to throttle jobs-processor in k8s: `kubectl -n prod set env deploy/jobs-processor MAX_WORKERS=10` — rolling restart.
jessica-sre: doing the env change now. `kubectl exec -it deploy/jobs-processor -n prod -- /bin/sh -c "ps aux | grep jobs"` — quick check after restart.
pagerduty-bot: Note: Escalation policy next in 9 minutes if unacknowledged — currently acked by marta.
marta: scaling redis: `kubectl -n infra scale statefulset redis-instant --replicas=4` — issuing now.
incident-bot: Autoscaling request queued: redis-instant scale -> 4. Expected warmup ~60s.
thomas: Also bumping pgbouncer max_client_conn from 1000 -> 1500 to accommodate extra pool pressure on the DB side. Command: `helm upgrade pgbouncer --set config.max_client_conn=1500` (helm values patched).
kai: Observability check: adding temporary dashboard with acceptqueue length and `net.peer.timeout` error rate.
marta: customer impact note: partial delivery delay for webhook consumers; some retries observed but no full customer-facing data loss. CS notified with templated message: "We're investigating intermittent webhook delivery delays and will follow up."
jessica-sre: jobs-processor restart completed, concurrency capped. I'm seeing retry rate drop from 450/s -> 60/s. Good.
incident-bot: Redis replica 4 entered Running state.
thomas: acceptqueue length dropping: 1200 -> 180 over 4m. Latency 99th now 45ms.
kai: 503s down to 0.4% — still above baseline but trending to normal.
marta: applying KV prefix cache for `user:session:*` keys (redis front). Patch: ```PATCH /services/cache-config
{ "prefix_cache": ["user:session:"] }``` This should reduce hits to accept queue for session validation path.
jessica-sre: patch applied. Cache hit ratio improving, TTL 30s.
oncall-manager: heads up — I'll need a handoff in 20m to day shift. Plan to file a short handoff note.
marta: will prepare handoff: what I will pass — root cause suspected: retry storm amplified by small transient redis throttling which caused client-side retries to pile up. Mitigations applied: concurrency limit, +1 redis replica, pgbouncer bump, prefix caching.
thomas: also found a scheduled job that misfired ~07:40 — `daily-sync` retried overlapping with traffic peak. Created issue: GH#5147 to add jitter.
kai: can we mute PD policy for 30m? Too noisy with multiple transient alerts.
marta: please don't mute globally; we'll add a PD suppression rule scoped to `redis-accept-queue` for 15m. thomas can apply.
thomas: suppression in PD applied for 15m.
pagerduty-bot: Suppression applied by thomas. Next escalation paused.
jessica-sre: FWIW I also rotated a problematic worker instance that had socket descriptor leak. `kubectl rollout restart deploy/worker-legacy -n prod`.
marta: monitoring 15m window. Current status summary: accept queue dropping, retry rate normalizing, customer 503s down. Impact: degraded webhook delivery (2.3% -> 0.4%), no data loss, CS notified. Next actions: observe 30m, follow up on GH#5147, add permanent rate limiter on jobs-processor.
incident-bot: Reminder: investigation log link https://logs.example/trace/PD#99823
thomas: I'll take handoff if you're stepping out. Prepared notes in the incident doc.
marta: handing off to thomas. Last check: acceptqueue ~90, 99p latency 38ms.
oncall-manager: thomas acknowledged handoff. Please update channel if any regressions.
thomas: oncall takeover accepted. Will keep PD incident open until stable for another 45m.
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD#99823 status: acknowledged, owners: marta, thomas, duration: ongoing.
(edited) thomas: small follow-up: added temporary alert threshold change to avoid page storms while we tune retry backoff: `alert.redis.acceptqueue.threshold=500` -> applied.
marta: thanks all. If stable at 45m we close and file postmortem.
last: thomas: resolution plan posted; will draft postmortem and action items. Closing update in ~1h unless regression.
